segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Hey, quick one on Northgate Labs. I'm cleaning up the renewal view in the CRM and the seat count is still showing 84, but their last invoice had 91 active users.

segments.speaker: Evan
segments.text: Yeah, that's because they added the pathology team in April. Billing tool has the overage at seven seats, prorated through July 31. It was like $3,220, nothing weird.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Got it. Their agreement ends next Wednesday and I don't think anyone has actually talked to them about carrying on yet.

segments.speaker: Evan
segments.text: Okay, then let's not send anything automated before we sanity check the account. Do they have any open support stuff that would make this touchy?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Two tickets, both closed. One was SSO mapping, one was a CSV export timing out. Customer success notes say their ops lead was happy after the fix.

segments.speaker: Evan
segments.text: Good. I'd propose we keep the same package, true them up to 91 seats, and ask if they want to go to 100 since they're adding the Denver site in September.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah. Pricing sheet puts 100 seats at $54,000 annual, standard support included. If they stay at 91 it's $49,140, so the step-up is pretty clean.

segments.speaker: Evan
segments.text: Let's draft it as a 12-month order form starting August 1, net 30, same terms. If procurement pushes on the start date, deal desk can adjust, but don't lead with that.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Makes sense. I'll call Jenna this afternoon and frame it around Denver onboarding, then follow with the order form if she's good with the seat band.

segments.speaker: Evan
segments.text: Perfect. Log the call notes in the CRM and tag me if she asks for a discount or a multi-year option.
